questions.question: In what year did the Industrial Revolution begin in Great Britain?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the Industrial Revolution began in Great Britain around 1760.
Incorrect. The article says the Industrial Revolution had spread to continental Europe and the United States by about 1840, not that it began then.
Incorrect. The year 1799 is mentioned as the earliest recorded use of the phrase "Industrial Revolution," not the start of the revolution itself.
Incorrect. The 1830s is when the term Industrial Revolution became more common, not when the revolution began.

questions.question: Which industry was the first to use modern production methods during the Industrial Revolution?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the textile industry was the first to use modern production methods.
Incorrect. Iron production is listed among new processes, but the article identifies textiles as the first industry to use modern production methods.
Incorrect. Steam power is described as an enabling technology, not the first industry to adopt modern production methods.
Incorrect. Chemical manufacturing is mentioned as part of the transition, but not as the first industry to use modern production methods.

questions.question: By what factor did mechanised cotton spinning increase output per worker?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that mechanised cotton spinning increased output per worker by a factor of around 500.
Incorrect. A factor of 40 is attributed to the power loom, not mechanised cotton spinning.
Incorrect. A factor of 50 is attributed to the cotton gin, not mechanised cotton spinning.
Incorrect. A factor of fifteen is attributed to the rolling mill compared with hammering wrought iron, not cotton spinning.

questions.question: Which country was the leading commercial nation by the mid-18th century?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that by the mid-18th century, Britain was the leading commercial nation.
Incorrect. France is mentioned in connection with the earliest recorded use of the term Industrial Revolution, not as the leading commercial nation.
Incorrect. The United States is mentioned as a destination of the Industrial Revolution's spread, not as the leading commercial nation in the mid-18th century.
Incorrect. China is mentioned as a prior center of manufacturing, not as the leading commercial nation by the mid-18th century.

questions.question: What did the substitution of coke for charcoal greatly lower in iron production?
options: the fuel cost of pig iron and wrought iron production
the speed of blast furnace operation
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that substituting coke for charcoal greatly lowered the fuel cost of pig iron and wrought iron production.
Incorrect. The article says coke allowed larger blast furnaces and economies of scale, not that it lowered the speed of operation.
Incorrect. The article notes steam engines were used to power blast air, but coke substitution did not remove the need for them.
Incorrect. The article does not state that coke substitution lowered demand for iron.

questions.question: What was the earliest recorded use of the phrase "Industrial Revolution"?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states the earliest recorded use of "Industrial Revolution" was in 1799 by French envoy Louis-Guillaume Otto.
Incorrect. Friedrich Engels wrote about an industrial revolution in 1844, but this was not the earliest recorded use.

questions.question: What happened to the share of cotton cloth manufactured in Britain that was exported between 1760 and 1800?
options: It rose from one-third to two-thirds
It fell from two-thirds to one-third
It rose from one-quarter to one-half
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that in 1760 approximately one-third of cotton cloth manufactured was exported, rising to two-thirds by 1800.
Incorrect. The article describes an increase, not a decrease, in the export share.
Incorrect. The article explicitly states the export share changed from one-third to two-thirds.
Incorrect. The article gives the figures as one-third and two-thirds, not one-quarter and one-half.

questions.question: Where did most manufacturing take place after the Industrial Revolution?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that after the Industrial Revolution, most manufacturing took place in North America and Western Europe.
Incorrect. The article says most manufacturing occurred in China and India prior to the Industrial Revolution, not after.
Incorrect. The article does not identify South America and Africa as the main manufacturing regions after the Industrial Revolution.
Incorrect. The article does not identify Russia and Japan as the main manufacturing regions after the Industrial Revolution.

questions.question: Which factor enabled industrialisation by freeing up labor and ensuring food surpluses?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that high agricultural productivity freed up labor and ensured food surpluses.
Incorrect. Political stability is listed as another enabling factor, but not the one that freed up labor and ensured food surpluses.
Incorrect. Abundant natural resources supported industrial growth but are not described as freeing up labor and ensuring food surpluses.
Incorrect. Access to financial capital played a crucial role but is not the factor described as freeing up labor and ensuring food surpluses.

questions.question: When did rapid growth reoccur after the recession of the late 1830s?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that rapid growth reoccurred after 1870, springing from new innovations in the Second Industrial Revolution.
Incorrect. High rates of growth in steam power and iron production occurred after 1800, but this was before the late 1830s recession.
Incorrect. The electrical telegraph was widely introduced in the 1840s but was not sufficient to drive high rates of growth.
Incorrect. The article does not identify 1850 as the point when rapid growth reoccurred.
